findings.title: Unbounded queue with no backpressure can exhaust memory
findings.body: In FixedQueuePool.__init__, the queues are created as `queue.Queue()` with no maxsize, making them unbounded. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit (line 293) calls `work_queue.put(work_item)` which never blocks. If a particular group is slow (e.g., a subscription whose handler hangs), all items for that group accumulate in its dedicated queue without limit. Unlike the existing `BatchStep`/`RunTask` strategies, this new strategy provides no backpressure: the main thread keeps fetching from Kafka and calling submit, so memory can grow without bound until the consumer OOMs. The PR description acknowledges that 'there's still a chance of individual items backlogging a queue' but does not bound the queue or block submit when queues are full.

findings.title: get_committable_offsets iterates O(max_offset) not O(outstanding)
findings.body: In OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets, the loop `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):` iterates over every offset in the numeric range, even those that were never added (e.g., gaps from compaction, filtered payloads, or pre-existing committed offsets). For a partition with min_offset=0 and max_offset=1_000_000 and only a few outstanding offsets, this is ~1 million iterations per call, and the commit loop calls this once per second per partition. It should iterate over the sorted `all_offsets` set (O(k log k) where k is the number of seen offsets) and break on the first outstanding/missing one.

findings.title: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join silently drops timeout argument
findings.body: `def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None: self.close()` ignores the `timeout` parameter entirely. Arroyo's ProcessingStrategy contract allows callers to pass a join timeout (e.g., during shutdown sequencing). Silently ignoring it means callers cannot bound how long join blocks, and the strategy will always wait the full internal 5.0s for the commit thread plus however long queue_pool.shutdown takes.

findings.title: FixedQueuePool.shutdown 5s join can drop in-flight work
findings.body: `worker.join(timeout=5.0)` only waits 5 seconds, and the worker is a daemon so it is killed on process exit. If a `result_processor` call takes longer than 5 seconds (which is exactly the kind of slow item this PR is designed to isolate), the join times out, the daemon thread is abandoned, and any work it was holding is never reported as completed/comitted. The fix is either to use a configurable/longer timeout, to join the strategy's commit thread only after all queues drain (e.g., call `wait_until_empty` first), or to set `immediate=True` on `q.shutdown()` and document the data-loss tradeoff.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the wrong behavior
findings.body: The test sets `mock_processor_call.side_effect = [Exception('Processing failed'), None]` and then asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. But OrderedQueueWorker.run catches the exception in the inner `except Exception` and still calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` in the `finally`, so offset 100 is marked completed. Offset 101 also completes. Both are contiguous, so the commit loop will commit offset 102 (101+1). The assertion as written would fail in the correct behavior, and the assertion is trivially true when `len == 0` regardless of what happened. The test should instead assert the committed offset reflects both completed messages (e.g., `committed_offsets[test_partition] == 102`) to actually verify the 'errors don't block other commits' intent.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown does not verify graceful behavior
findings.body: The test submits 5 messages and then immediately calls `factory.shutdown()` without waiting for processing, asserting only `factory.queue_pool is None`. This does not verify that the 5 submitted messages are processed before shutdown, that no offsets are lost, or that the shutdown is actually graceful. Combined with the 5s join timeout in FixedQueuePool.shutdown, this test will pass even if shutdown drops all in-flight work.

findings.title: Kafka integration test depends on private StreamProcessor internals
findings.body: The test drives the consumer by calling `processor._run_once()` in a loop and `processor._shutdown()` at the end. These are private arroyo methods (leading underscore) and are not part of the public API; they can change between arroyo releases without notice, which would silently break this test. It also relies on `override_settings(KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES=...)` and creates real Kafka topics in a `requires_kafka` test, so it is expensive and fragile. A more robust integration test would use the public `run()` method or otherwise not depend on underscore-prefixed methods.

findings.title: Unreachable queue.ShutDown handler in inner try
findings.body: The inner `try` block in OrderedQueueWorker.run only wraps `sentry_sdk.start_transaction(...)` and `self.result_processor(...)`. `queue.ShutDown` can only be raised by `queue.Queue.get()` or `queue.Queue.put()`, neither of which is called inside this inner try. The `except queue.ShutDown: break` on lines 142-143 is therefore dead code and can be removed (or, if a put call is later added inside the inner try, the comment should explain why).
